challenges.name: swallowed-exceptions-statements
challenges.title: Swallowed exceptions: what the catch blocks do
challenges.description: Two statements about the enrollment-with-payment code an AI assistant wrote for premium courses: what happens to a learner whose card is declined, and when catching an error without rethrowing it is the right call.

questions.explanation: False. chargeLearner catches the PaymentDeclinedError and returns null, so enrollWithPayment never sees a failure: it activates the enrollment with chargeId null and returns status "enrolled". The learner gets the course for free, and because the catch neither logs nor rethrows, nothing in the logs or the error tracker shows it - finance finds it a month later in reconciliation. A catch that turns an error into null or [] does not handle the error, it changes its meaning. The misconception is that wrapping a call in try/catch makes code safer; here it is what made the failure invisible.

True. The rule is not "never catch"; it is "never hide". At this point the money is captured and the enrollment is active, so failing the request would tell a learner who paid that something went wrong and invite a second payment. The receipt is a side effect that can be retried, so the code decides the outcome deliberately (the learner is enrolled) and keeps the evidence (a warn line with the enrollment, the learner, the course and the reason) that support or a retry job can act on. Compare it with the AI's catch { } on the same call: same control flow, but nothing tells anyone that a receipt was never sent. The misconception is to judge a catch block by whether it rethrows instead of by whether the failure is still visible and the outcome is correct.

challenges.name: swallowed-exceptions-failed-payment
challenges.title: Swallowed exceptions: the payment that failed silently
challenges.description:
An AI coding assistant wrote the enrollment flow for premium courses on CodeDev from the request "create the enrollment, charge the learner's payment method, activate the enrollment and email a receipt. Handle errors." Finance's monthly reconciliation found 23 learners with an active premium enrollment and no captured payment, and the logs have no line about any of them.

Fix enrollWithPayment(req, deps):
- Insert the enrollment (it starts pending), charge req.paymentMethodId for req.priceVnd with the enrollment id as idempotencyKey, activate the enrollment with the charge id, then send the receipt.
- PaymentDeclinedError from the gateway: remove the enrollment, call logger.warn("payment_declined", context) with reason = the error's code, and return { status: "payment_declined", code }.
- Any other error from the gateway: remove the enrollment, call logger.error("payment_failed", context) with reason = the error's message, and throw the same error.
- The receipt email fails: the learner stays enrolled; call logger.warn("receipt_failed", context) with reason = the error's message and return { status: "enrolled", enrollmentId }.
- DuplicateEnrollmentError from insert: let it propagate; nothing is charged.
Every log context is { enrollmentId, userId, courseId, reason }; log nothing on success.

The file contains an in-memory enrollments table, a fake gateway that behaves by payment method id (pm_ok..., pm_declined_<code>, pm_timeout, pm_broken), a mailer that bounces the users listed in the test, and a runner that processes the test's requests in order and prints each outcome (or the error it threw), every log line, the remaining enrollment rows and the captured charges. Do not change the error classes, the types, the fakes or the runner.
hints: When the gateway declines a card, what value does chargeLearner return, and what does enrollWithPayment do with that value next? Who finds out that the charge failed?

Look at the two catch blocks: the one in chargeLearner that returns null and the empty one around sendReceipt. For each, decide what the outcome should be (map, rethrow or continue), what must be undone (the pending row), and what must be left behind as evidence (a log line with its context).

A similar case on another flow: issuing a certificate. try { pdf = await renderer.render(id) } catch (error) { await certificates.remove(id); if (error instanceof TemplateMissingError) { logger.warn("certificate_template_missing", ctx(error.template)); return { status: "not_issued" }; } logger.error("certificate_failed", ctx(error.message)); throw error; } - the expected failure is mapped to a result, the unexpected one is rethrown, both undo the partial row and both are logged with context.
